correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge3\), \(1\le k\le n\) and \(\lambda>0\), conditional on any frontier-direction sequence and an internal seed, exactly \((\ell-m-1)_+\) positions survive \(m\) infection events. Uniform seeding gives the event-rank tail, and two frontier hazards give independent \(\operatorname{Exp}(2\lambda)\) event intervals. Poissonization gives the complete detection-time survival function, and its exact positive second discrete difference \(e^{-u}u^{\ell-1}/(\ell-1)!\) yields sharp balanced/concentrated gap extrema. Both boundary cases and the expectation formula are derived; a separate 50,036-assertion exact verifier cross-checks small-cycle transition equations and gap ranks without being presented as an infinite proof.

The available broader results therefore are not dominating mathematical implications.

originality.rationale: The motivating KDD 2007 paper provides general submodular approximation for outbreak detection, and arXiv:2011.01998 studies adaptive epidemic test placement. Inspected relevant primary material does not state or imply this exact uniform detection-event rank or strict all-time stochastic-optimal placement theorem. Semantic research-record comparisons using aliases, the Poisson transform and sensor-gap formulations found no directly covering record. Priority remains provisional because obscure exact ring surveillance literature may exist and some plausible historical full texts were inaccessible. Colman et al. (2019) full primary publisher text presents spatially dispersed sentinel heuristics and SIR simulations rather than an exact homogeneous SI cycle all-time rank theorem.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional: not every older network-sentinel, one-dimensional contact-process, and mathematical surveillance source was accessible or indexed.
The Christakis–Fowler full text and the 2012 incidence-at-detection paper full text were not established; no blanket assertion of noncoverage by those whole papers is made.
The 2007 technical report is dated June without a verified day; the earliest precisely verified public date for the selected primary published paper is August 12, 2007.
The full text of Holme (2018), arXiv:1803.10637, was not accessible in this run; its abstract is related, but no decisive exact-cycle overlap is suggested by the available material.

value.rationale: The source-unknown detection-placement question is natural in epidemic surveillance, and the theorem solves the complete finite-cycle design problem simultaneously for every positive time and all increasing delay losses. It supplies both exact best and worst placements, an unexpected conditional uniform infection-event rank, and an explicit full distribution, whereas prior general frameworks typically give approximate optimization. It is a scientifically motivated idealized benchmark, not a claim of direct field applicability.
